correctness.rationale: The scalar oracle \(\widehat{\mathbb F}(x;\xi)=Lx+\xi\) is unbiased and its paired sample difference is exactly \(L(x-y)\), so it satisfies the required cocoercivity-in-expectation assumption. With \(\alpha=2/L\), the deterministic map is \(-I\). Direct solution of the two linear stochastic recurrences yields the displayed terminal noise-transfer coefficients. Independence removes cross terms, and multiplication by \(L^2=4/\alpha^2\) gives the residual laws. The finite Dual-OHM coefficient sum tends to \(\pi^2/4-1\) by the standard odd reciprocal-square identity. The packaged exact-rational replay independently reconstructs both recurrences for horizons through \(24\).

value.rationale: The reflection \(\mathbb T=-I\) is the extremal noncontractive endpoint of the source's admissible scalar cocoercive family, so it is a natural stress test rather than an arbitrary slice. The theorem exactly quantifies the paper's central robustness claim on this boundary: fixed-batch Dual-OHM has a finite zeta-valued noise floor while the matched stochastic OHM residual variance grows linearly. This supplies a reusable closed-form benchmark, isolates actual stochastic transfer rather than proof-weight heuristics, and shows that the experimentally observed anchor instability is already present in one dimension.
